definition: A plan, drawing, structure, or arrangement created for a particular purpose; as a verb, to create such a plan.

mnemonic.root_memory: DESIGNARE = mark out; design marks out how something should be made.
mnemonic.story_en: The architect used a DESIGN to mark out every part of the building before construction.
mnemonic.story_zh: 建築師用「設計（DESIGN）」在施工前標示出建築每個部分。

example: The design of the app makes it easy for users to compare vocabulary cards.
example_zh: 這個應用程式的設計讓使用者容易比較單字卡。

near_synonyms.difference: a plan can be general; a design usually includes structure and intended form.
style is appearance; design includes function and structure.

usage_note: design is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Used to show that something happens or is true although another fact might have prevented it.

mnemonic.root_memory: DESPIT suggests defiance; despite means something remains true in defiance of difficulty.
mnemonic.story_en: DESPITE heavy rain, the team continued the outdoor experiment.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「儘管（DESPITE）」下著大雨，團隊仍繼續戶外實驗。

example: Despite limited funding, the researchers completed the survey on time.
example_zh: 儘管資金有限，研究人員仍準時完成調查。

near_synonyms.difference: although introduces a full clause; despite is followed by a noun phrase or gerund.
however links contrasting sentences; despite introduces a contrast within one structure.

usage_note: despite is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To discover or notice something, especially something hidden, faint, or difficult to observe.

mnemonic.root_memory: DE + TEGERE = uncover; detect means discovering what was covered.
mnemonic.story_en: The sensor DETECTED smoke before anyone could see the fire.
mnemonic.story_zh: 感測器在任何人看到火前就「偵測（DETECT）」到煙。

example: The test can detect early signs of infection before symptoms appear.
example_zh: 這項檢測能在症狀出現前偵測感染早期跡象。

near_synonyms.difference: notice can be casual; detect often implies hidden or subtle evidence.
identify means name what it is; detect means discover its presence.

usage_note: detect is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A tool, machine, or piece of equipment made for a particular purpose; also a method used to achieve an effect.

mnemonic.root_memory: A device is something devised or arranged for a purpose.
mnemonic.story_en: The engineer built a DEVICE to measure air quality inside classrooms.
mnemonic.story_zh: 工程師製作一個「裝置（DEVICE）」來測量教室內空氣品質。

example: Wearable devices can track heart rate and sleep patterns.
example_zh: 穿戴式裝置可以追蹤心率與睡眠模式。

near_synonyms.difference: a machine is usually larger or mechanical; a device can be small, digital, or conceptual.
instrument often measures or performs precise work; device is broader.

usage_note: device is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To give time, energy, attention, or resources to a person, purpose, or activity.

mnemonic.root_memory: VOVERE = vow; devote means giving yourself by commitment.
mnemonic.story_en: She DEVOTED two years to researching rural education.
mnemonic.story_zh: 她「投入（DEVOTE）」兩年研究鄉村教育。

example: The organization devotes most of its budget to community health programs.
example_zh: 該組織把大部分預算投入社區健康計畫。

near_synonyms.difference: dedicate is very close; devote often stresses sustained time or effort.
allocate means assign resources; devote suggests commitment.

usage_note: devote is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A measurable aspect such as length, width, or depth; also an important feature or aspect of a situation.

mnemonic.root_memory: MENS = measure; a dimension is something measured or considered as an aspect.
mnemonic.story_en: The designer measured every DIMENSION before building the model.
mnemonic.story_zh: 設計師在製作模型前測量每個「尺寸（DIMENSION）」。

example: The debate has an ethical dimension that cannot be ignored.
example_zh: 這場辯論有一個不可忽視的倫理面向。

near_synonyms.difference: aspect is a feature; dimension often implies a measurable or analytical aspect.
size is general amount; dimension is a specific measurement or perspective.

usage_note: dimension is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Related to the home, family, or one’s own country rather than foreign affairs.

mnemonic.root_memory: DOMUS = home; domestic matters belong to home or country.
mnemonic.story_en: The report compared DOMESTIC demand with exports to foreign markets.
mnemonic.story_zh: 報告比較「國內（DOMESTIC）」需求與外銷市場。

example: Domestic tourism increased when international travel became more expensive.
example_zh: 國際旅行變貴後，國內旅遊增加。

near_synonyms.difference: national relates to the country; domestic contrasts with foreign or international.
household concerns a home; domestic can also mean national.

usage_note: domestic is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To have the most power, influence, attention, or control in a situation.

mnemonic.root_memory: DOMINARI = rule; dominate means having ruling influence.
mnemonic.story_en: One company DOMINATED the market after buying its largest competitor.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一家公司買下最大競爭者後「主導（DOMINATE）」市場。

example: Economic concerns dominated the election debate.
example_zh: 經濟議題主導了選舉辯論。

near_synonyms.difference: control means direct; dominate suggests superior power or influence.
lead can be positive guidance; dominate can imply overwhelming influence.

usage_note: dominate is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: An early version of a text, plan, or law; as a verb, to write an early version or select someone for service.

mnemonic.root_memory: DRAFT is drawn out first before the final version.
mnemonic.story_en: The writer revised the first DRAFT three times before submission.
mnemonic.story_zh: 作者在提交前把第一份「草稿（DRAFT）」修改三次。

example: The committee circulated a draft of the policy for public comment.
example_zh: 委員會傳閱政策草案以徵詢公眾意見。

near_synonyms.difference: an outline is a structure; a draft is a fuller early version.
a proposal suggests action; a draft may be any unfinished text.

usage_note: draft is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: The system by which goods, services, money, labor, and resources are produced and exchanged.

mnemonic.root_memory: OIKOS + NOMOS = household management; economy is resource management at scale.
mnemonic.story_en: A national ECONOMY manages resources like a huge household.
mnemonic.story_zh: 國家「經濟（ECONOMY）」像大型家庭一樣管理資源。

example: The economy grew slowly as exports weakened and consumer spending fell.
example_zh: 出口轉弱、消費支出下降後，經濟成長放慢。

near_synonyms.difference: a market is where exchange occurs; economy is the whole production and exchange system.
finance concerns money management; economy is broader.

usage_note: economy is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A basic part of a whole, system, argument, or substance.

mnemonic.root_memory: ELEMENTUM = basic principle; an element is a basic part.
mnemonic.story_en: Trust is an essential ELEMENT of successful cooperation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 信任是成功合作的基本「要素（ELEMENT）」。

example: The plan includes every element needed for a safe evacuation.
example_zh: 該計畫包含安全疏散所需的每個要素。

near_synonyms.difference: component often belongs to a working system; element is any basic part.
factor influences a result; element is a constituent part.

usage_note: element is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To remove or get rid of something completely, especially a problem, risk, or competitor.

mnemonic.root_memory: EX + LIMEN = push out past the threshold; eliminate means remove.
mnemonic.story_en: The new filter ELIMINATED harmful particles from the water.
mnemonic.story_zh: 新濾網從水中「去除（ELIMINATE）」有害微粒。

example: The policy aims to eliminate unnecessary paperwork for small businesses.
example_zh: 該政策旨在消除小企業不必要的文書作業。

near_synonyms.difference: remove is broad; eliminate suggests complete removal.
reduce makes less; eliminate removes entirely.

usage_note: eliminate is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To come into view, become known, or develop as something new or important.

mnemonic.root_memory: E + MERGE = come out from being submerged; emerge means appear.
mnemonic.story_en: New evidence EMERGED during the investigation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 調查期間新證據「浮現（EMERGE）」。

example: Several patterns emerged after researchers compared the interview data.
example_zh: 研究人員比較訪談資料後，幾個模式浮現出來。

near_synonyms.difference: appear is general; emerge often suggests gradual appearance after being hidden.
develop stresses growth; emerge stresses becoming visible or known.

usage_note: emerge is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Special importance, attention, or force given to something.

mnemonic.root_memory: EMPHAINEIN = show clearly; emphasis makes something stand out.
mnemonic.story_en: The teacher placed EMPHASIS on evidence-based writing.
mnemonic.story_zh: 老師「強調（EMPHASIS）」以證據為基礎的寫作。

example: The program places strong emphasis on practical communication skills.
example_zh: 該課程非常強調實用溝通能力。

near_synonyms.difference: stress is very close; emphasis is often a noun for special attention.
focus is attention; emphasis adds importance or force.

usage_note: emphasis is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: The capacity to do work, produce heat, power activity, or sustain physical and mental effort.

mnemonic.root_memory: ENERGEIA = activity; energy powers action.
mnemonic.story_en: Solar panels convert sunlight into usable ENERGY.
mnemonic.story_zh: 太陽能板把陽光轉換成可用「能源（ENERGY）」。

example: The city is investing in renewable energy to reduce carbon emissions.
example_zh: 該城市投資再生能源以減少碳排放。

near_synonyms.difference: power is usable force or authority; energy is capacity to do work.
fuel is a material source; energy is the output or capacity.

usage_note: energy is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: The natural world or the surrounding conditions in which a person, organization, or system exists.
definition_zh: 環境；周遭條件；自然環境

mnemonic.story_en: A healthy ENVIRONMENT supports both people and ecosystems.
mnemonic.story_zh: 健康的「環境（ENVIRONMENT）」支持人類與生態系。
mnemonic.root_memory: ENVIRON = around, surrounding; connect this root idea with environment.

example: A supportive learning environment can improve student confidence.
example_zh: 支持性的學習環境能提升學生信心。

near_synonyms.difference: setting is the place or situation; environment includes broader conditions.
ecosystem is biological; environment can be social, work-related, or natural.

usage_note: environment is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To consider or describe two things as the same or equal in meaning, value, or effect.

mnemonic.story_en: The article warned readers not to EQUATE correlation with causation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 文章提醒讀者不要把相關「等同於（EQUATE）」因果。
mnemonic.root_memory: AEQUUS = equal, even; connect this root idea with equate.

example: High income should not be equated with personal happiness.
example_zh: 高收入不應被等同於個人幸福。

near_synonyms.difference: compare examines similarity or difference; equate treats as equal.
associate links ideas; equate makes them equivalent.

usage_note: equate is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A mistake, incorrect action, or difference between a measured value and the true value.

mnemonic.story_en: A small ERROR in the formula changed the final result.
mnemonic.story_zh: 公式中的小「錯誤（ERROR）」改變了最終結果。
mnemonic.root_memory: ERRARE = to wander, go astray; connect this root idea with error.

example: The system records each error so engineers can improve reliability.
example_zh: 系統記錄每個錯誤，使工程師能提升可靠性。

near_synonyms.difference: mistake is general; error is common in technical and analytical contexts.
fault may imply responsibility; error may simply be incorrectness.

usage_note: error is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: All the money, property, and possessions belonging to a person, especially after death; also a large area of land.

mnemonic.story_en: The lawyer managed the ESTATE after the owner died.
mnemonic.story_zh: 所有者過世後，律師管理其「遺產（ESTATE）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: STATUS = state, condition; connect this root idea with estate.

example: The family sold part of the estate to pay inheritance taxes.
example_zh: 該家庭出售部分遺產以支付遺產稅。

near_synonyms.difference: property is broad; estate often refers to total assets or land.
assets are things of value; estate is the legal whole of possessions.

usage_note: estate is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Related to a group of people who share cultural traditions, ancestry, language, or national background.

mnemonic.story_en: The festival celebrated the city’s ETHNIC diversity.
mnemonic.story_zh: 節慶慶祝城市的「族群（ETHNIC）」多樣性。
mnemonic.root_memory: ETHNOS = nation, people; connect this root idea with ethnic.

example: The survey collected data on age, income, and ethnic background.
example_zh: 調查蒐集年齡、收入與族群背景資料。

near_synonyms.difference: racial refers to socially constructed race; ethnic emphasizes culture and ancestry.
cultural is broader; ethnic refers to group identity and heritage.

usage_note: ethnic is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Happening at the end of a process or after a period of time.

mnemonic.story_en: After many delays, the EVENTUAL decision surprised the public.
mnemonic.story_zh: 多次延宕後，「最終的（EVENTUAL）」決定讓大眾驚訝。
mnemonic.root_memory: EVENTUS = outcome, result; connect this root idea with eventual.

example: The eventual success of the program depended on community support.
example_zh: 該計畫最終成功取決於社區支持。

near_synonyms.difference: final means last; eventual stresses happening after time or delay.
ultimate means last or most important; eventual is more time-based.

usage_note: eventual is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Information, facts, objects, or signs that help prove whether something is true.

mnemonic.story_en: The fingerprints were strong EVIDENCE in the investigation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 指紋是調查中的有力「證據（EVIDENCE）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: EVIDENS = obvious, clear; connect this root idea with evidence.

example: There is little evidence that the policy improved student achievement.
example_zh: 幾乎沒有證據顯示該政策提升了學生表現。

near_synonyms.difference: proof is stronger and more conclusive; evidence may support without proving fully.
indication is a sign; evidence is used to support a claim.

usage_note: evidence is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To develop gradually over time, especially from a simpler to a more complex or different form.

mnemonic.story_en: The software EVOLVED from a small tool into a full platform.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這套軟體從小工具「演變（EVOLVE）」成完整平台。
mnemonic.root_memory: EX = out; connect this root idea with evolve.

example: Language evolves as speakers create new words and meanings.
example_zh: 語言會隨著使用者創造新字與新意義而演變。

near_synonyms.difference: develop is broad; evolve stresses gradual change over time.
adapt means adjust to conditions; evolve may happen across generations or stages.

usage_note: evolve is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A noticeable quality, part, or function of something; as a verb, to include or give special attention to something.

mnemonic.story_en: The app’s best FEATURE is its simple review mode.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這個應用程式最好的「功能（FEATURE）」是簡單的複習模式。
mnemonic.root_memory: FACTURA = form, formation; connect this root idea with feature.

example: The report features interviews with workers from several industries.
example_zh: 該報告以來自多個產業工人的訪談為特色。

near_synonyms.difference: characteristic is a trait; feature is a noticeable part or function.
function is what something does; feature may be a visible quality or function.

usage_note: feature is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Coming at the end of a process, series, or decision; not expected to be changed.
definition_zh: 最後的；最終的；決定性的

mnemonic.story_en: The FINAL version of the report was sent to the board.
mnemonic.story_zh: 報告的「最終（FINAL）」版本已送交董事會。
mnemonic.root_memory: FINIS = end, boundary; connect this root idea with final.

example: The final decision will be announced after the public hearing.
example_zh: 最終決定將在公開聽證會後宣布。

near_synonyms.difference: last simply means after all others; final can imply official completion.
conclusive means settling doubt; final means ending a process.

usage_note: final is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: The management of money, credit, investment, and funding by individuals, businesses, or governments.

mnemonic.root_memory: FINIS relates to settlement; finance concerns how money is settled and managed.
mnemonic.story_en: The startup needed FINANCE before it could build its product.
mnemonic.story_zh: 新創公司需要「資金／財務（FINANCE）」才能開發產品。

example: Public finance determines how governments raise and spend money.
example_zh: 公共財政決定政府如何籌措與支出資金。

near_synonyms.difference: funding is money provided; finance is the broader system or field.
economics studies production and markets; finance focuses on money and investment.

usage_note: finance is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: The main point of attention, interest, or activity; as a verb, to direct attention or effort.

mnemonic.root_memory: FOCUS was the hearth at the center; focus is the center of attention.
mnemonic.story_en: The FOCUS of the meeting was how to improve student support.
mnemonic.story_zh: 會議的「焦點（FOCUS）」是如何改善學生支持。

example: The study focuses on how sleep affects memory.
example_zh: 該研究聚焦於睡眠如何影響記憶。

near_synonyms.difference: emphasis means special importance; focus means central attention.
topic is a subject; focus is the main point within it.

usage_note: focus is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A fixed rule, mathematical expression, recipe, or method used to produce a result.

mnemonic.root_memory: FORMA = form; a formula gives a fixed form for producing an answer.
mnemonic.story_en: The scientist used a FORMULA to calculate the chemical concentration.
mnemonic.story_zh: 科學家用「公式（FORMULA）」計算化學濃度。

example: There is no simple formula for building trust in a divided community.
example_zh: 在分裂的社群中建立信任沒有簡單公式。

near_synonyms.difference: an equation states mathematical equality; a formula can be any fixed rule or recipe.
method is a way of doing something; formula is more fixed.

usage_note: formula is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A group of people born around the same time; also the production or creation of something.

mnemonic.root_memory: GEN = birth; a generation is a group born in the same period.
mnemonic.story_en: Each GENERATION inherits problems and creates new solutions.
mnemonic.story_zh: 每個「世代（GENERATION）」都承接問題並創造新解方。

example: Renewable energy generation increased after new solar farms opened.
example_zh: 新太陽能農場啟用後，再生能源發電量增加。

near_synonyms.difference: cohort is a defined group in research; generation is broader and social.
production is creation; generation can mean creation or age group.

usage_note: generation is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Money received from work, investments, business, or government support over a period of time.

mnemonic.root_memory: IN + COME = money that comes in.
mnemonic.story_en: Monthly INCOME determines how much a household can save.
mnemonic.story_zh: 每月「收入（INCOME）」決定家庭能儲蓄多少。

example: The policy provides tax relief for families with low income.
example_zh: 該政策為低收入家庭提供稅務減免。

near_synonyms.difference: revenue is money received by a business or government; income often refers to individuals or households.
salary is regular pay from employment; income includes all sources.

usage_note: income is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To point out, show, or suggest something, often through evidence, signs, or data.

mnemonic.root_memory: DICARE = point out; indicate means showing what something means.
mnemonic.story_en: The chart INDICATED a steady rise in energy demand.
mnemonic.story_zh: 圖表「顯示（INDICATE）」能源需求穩定上升。

example: Survey results indicate that most users prefer shorter lessons.
example_zh: 調查結果顯示，多數使用者偏好較短課程。

near_synonyms.difference: suggest is less direct; indicate can be based on signs or evidence.
prove is conclusive; indicate only points toward a conclusion.

usage_note: indicate is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Related to one person or thing considered separately from a group; as a noun, a single person.

mnemonic.root_memory: INDIVIDUAL originally means not divided; one separate person or thing.
mnemonic.story_en: Each INDIVIDUAL response was coded before the survey results were combined.
mnemonic.story_zh: 每份「個別的（INDIVIDUAL）」回覆在合併調查結果前都先編碼。

example: The teacher adjusted feedback to each student’s individual needs.
example_zh: 老師依每位學生的個別需求調整回饋。

near_synonyms.difference: personal relates to a person; individual stresses separate from a group.
distinct means clearly different; individual means considered one by one.

usage_note: individual is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Happening at the beginning of a process, period, or series.

mnemonic.root_memory: INITIUM = beginning; initial means at the start.
mnemonic.story_en: The INITIAL results were promising but not final.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「初步（INITIAL）」結果令人期待，但尚非最終結果。

example: Initial feedback from users helped the team redesign the interface.
example_zh: 使用者的初步回饋幫助團隊重新設計介面。

near_synonyms.difference: preliminary means before final; initial simply means first.
early is broad; initial marks the starting point.

usage_note: initial is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A particular example, case, or occurrence of something.

mnemonic.root_memory: STARE = stand; an instance stands as one example.
mnemonic.story_en: The report gave one INSTANCE of successful community cooperation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 報告提供一個成功社區合作的「實例（INSTANCE）」。

example: In this instance, the company responded quickly to customer complaints.
example_zh: 在這個情況中，公司快速回應顧客投訴。

near_synonyms.difference: example is general; instance often refers to one occurrence of a broader pattern.
case can be legal or analytical; instance stresses one example.

usage_note: instance is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Detailed information about how to do something; also the act of teaching or directing.

mnemonic.root_memory: STRUCT = build; instruction builds knowledge or guides action.
mnemonic.story_en: Clear INSTRUCTIONS helped the team assemble the equipment safely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 清楚的「指示（INSTRUCTIONS）」幫助團隊安全組裝設備。

example: Participants received written instructions before beginning the experiment.
example_zh: 參與者在開始實驗前收到書面說明。

near_synonyms.difference: directions tell what to do; instruction can include teaching or detailed guidance.
education is broad; instruction is the teaching process or specific directions.

usage_note: instruction is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To put money, time, effort, or resources into something in order to gain a future benefit.

mnemonic.root_memory: INVEST originally meant clothe or endow; now it means putting resources into future value.
mnemonic.story_en: The company INVESTED in training to improve employee skills.
mnemonic.story_zh: 公司「投資（INVEST）」培訓以提升員工技能。

example: Governments invest in infrastructure to support long-term economic growth.
example_zh: 政府投資基礎建設以支持長期經濟成長。

near_synonyms.difference: fund means provide money; invest implies expected future return.
spend uses resources; invest uses them for future benefit.

usage_note: invest is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Related to law or permitted by law.

mnemonic.root_memory: LEGIS = law; legal things are connected to law.
mnemonic.story_en: The company sought LEGAL advice before signing the contract.
mnemonic.story_zh: 公司在簽約前尋求「法律（LEGAL）」建議。

example: The new rules created legal uncertainty for small businesses.
example_zh: 新規則給小企業帶來法律不確定性。

near_synonyms.difference: lawful means permitted by law; legal can mean related to law or lawful.
legitimate can mean valid or acceptable; legal specifically concerns law.

usage_note: legal is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To make or pass laws through an official lawmaking process.

mnemonic.root_memory: LEGIS + LAT = bring law; legislate means creating laws.
mnemonic.story_en: Parliament LEGISLATED to reduce pollution from factories.
mnemonic.story_zh: 國會「立法（LEGISLATE）」以減少工廠污染。

example: Governments cannot legislate trust, but they can create fair procedures.
example_zh: 政府無法立法創造信任，但能建立公平程序。

near_synonyms.difference: enact means officially pass a law; legislate describes the broader lawmaking activity.
regulate controls behavior; legislate creates legal rules.

usage_note: legislate is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A system of reasoning used to reach valid conclusions; also the principles that make an argument or process sensible.

mnemonic.root_memory: LOGOS = reason; logic is structured reasoning.
mnemonic.story_en: The professor checked the LOGIC of the student’s argument.
mnemonic.story_zh: 教授檢查學生論點的「邏輯（LOGIC）」。

example: The logic of the policy is clear, but implementation remains difficult.
example_zh: 該政策的邏輯很清楚，但執行仍然困難。

near_synonyms.difference: reasoning is the process; logic is the system or structure behind it.
rationale is the reason for a decision; logic is broader reasoning structure.

usage_note: logic is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To keep something in a particular state, continue doing it, or state that something is true.

mnemonic.root_memory: MANUS + TENERE = hold in hand; maintain means keep hold of a state.
mnemonic.story_en: The technician MAINTAINED the machines to prevent breakdowns.
mnemonic.story_zh: 技術員「維護（MAINTAIN）」機器以避免故障。

example: Researchers maintained that the sample was large enough for analysis.
example_zh: 研究人員主張樣本數足以進行分析。

near_synonyms.difference: preserve protects from change; maintain keeps something operating or continuing.
claim states something; maintain suggests continuing to assert it.

usage_note: maintain is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Important, large, or serious in scale or effect; as a noun, a main field of study.

mnemonic.root_memory: MAJOR = greater; major things are larger or more important.
mnemonic.story_en: A MAJOR storm disrupted transport across the region.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一場「重大（MAJOR）」風暴中斷了該地區交通。

example: Air pollution remains a major concern for urban residents.
example_zh: 空氣污染仍是都市居民的主要關切。

near_synonyms.difference: important stresses value; major often stresses scale or impact.
primary means first or main; major means large or important.

usage_note: major is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Systems, organizations, or channels used to communicate information to the public; plural of medium.

mnemonic.root_memory: MEDIUM = middle; media carry messages between senders and audiences.
mnemonic.story_en: Social MEDIA changed how citizens receive political news.
mnemonic.story_zh: 社群「媒體（MEDIA）」改變公民接收政治新聞的方式。

example: The campaign used both traditional media and online platforms.
example_zh: 該活動同時使用傳統媒體與線上平台。

near_synonyms.difference: press usually means news organizations; media includes many communication channels.
platform is one channel or service; media is broader.

usage_note: media is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Related to the mind, thought, emotions, or psychological health.

mnemonic.root_memory: MENS = mind; mental things belong to the mind.
mnemonic.story_en: MENTAL health is as important as physical health.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「心理（MENTAL）」健康和身體健康一樣重要。

example: Long working hours can affect both physical and mental well-being.
example_zh: 長時間工作可能同時影響身體與心理福祉。

near_synonyms.difference: psychological often concerns emotions or behavior; mental is broader.
cognitive concerns thinking; mental includes emotion and thought.

usage_note: mental is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A planned way of doing something, especially one that follows an organized procedure.

mnemonic.root_memory: METHODOS = way of pursuit; a method is an organized way to proceed.
mnemonic.story_en: The researcher chose a METHOD that could be repeated by other teams.
mnemonic.story_zh: 研究人員選擇一種其他團隊可重複的「方法（METHOD）」。

example: The method section explains how participants were selected.
example_zh: 方法章節說明參與者如何被選取。

near_synonyms.difference: approach is broader and more flexible; method is more systematic.
technique is a specific skill or procedure; method can be a broader plan.

usage_note: method is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A connected system of people, organizations, computers, roads, or relationships.

mnemonic.root_memory: NET + WORK = a working web of connections.
mnemonic.story_en: A strong professional NETWORK helped her find research partners.
mnemonic.story_zh: 強大的專業「人脈網絡（NETWORK）」幫她找到研究夥伴。

example: The hospital network shares patient data through a secure platform.
example_zh: 該醫院網絡透過安全平台共享病患資料。

near_synonyms.difference: system is organized parts; network stresses connections between nodes.
community stresses shared identity; network stresses links.

usage_note: network is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Usual, expected, or conforming to a standard; not abnormal or unusual.

mnemonic.root_memory: NORMA = rule; normal fits the standard rule or pattern.
mnemonic.story_en: The patient’s temperature returned to NORMAL by morning.
mnemonic.story_zh: 病人的體溫到早上恢復「正常（NORMAL）」。

example: It is normal for demand to rise before major holidays.
example_zh: 重大節日前需求上升是正常的。

near_synonyms.difference: typical means representative; normal means expected or within standard range.
standard is an accepted norm; normal describes what fits it.

usage_note: normal is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: One of the choices available in a situation or decision.

mnemonic.root_memory: OPTARE = choose; an option is something you can choose.
mnemonic.story_en: The menu offered a vegetarian OPTION for guests.
mnemonic.story_zh: 菜單為客人提供素食「選項（OPTION）」。

example: Students have the option to submit either a report or a presentation.
example_zh: 學生可以選擇提交報告或簡報。

near_synonyms.difference: alternative is another possible choice; option is any available choice.
possibility may be theoretical; option is usually actionable.

usage_note: option is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Something produced by a person, machine, system, or process; also the amount produced.

mnemonic.root_memory: OUTPUT is what a system puts out.
mnemonic.story_en: The factory increased OUTPUT after upgrading its equipment.
mnemonic.story_zh: 工廠升級設備後提高「產出（OUTPUT）」。

example: The model’s output must be checked for errors before publication.
example_zh: 模型輸出在發布前必須檢查錯誤。

near_synonyms.difference: result is broad; output is what a process or system produces.
product is an item for sale; output can be data, energy, or production amount.

usage_note: output is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Considering everything or everyone together; total rather than partial.

mnemonic.root_memory: OVER + ALL = across the whole; overall means total or general.
mnemonic.story_en: The OVERALL result improved even though one section performed poorly.
mnemonic.story_zh: 雖然有一部分表現不佳，但「整體（OVERALL）」結果改善了。

example: Overall satisfaction increased after the service was redesigned.
example_zh: 服務重新設計後，整體滿意度提高。

near_synonyms.difference: general may be broad or unspecific; overall means considering all parts.
total is numerical or complete; overall can be evaluative.

usage_note: overall is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A person, organization, or country that shares an activity, relationship, responsibility, or business interest with another.

mnemonic.root_memory: PART = share; partners share work, risk, or relationship.
mnemonic.story_en: The university found an industry PARTNER for the research project.
mnemonic.story_zh: 大學為研究專案找到產業「合作夥伴（PARTNER）」。

example: Local partners helped the organization understand community needs.
example_zh: 地方夥伴協助該組織了解社區需求。

near_synonyms.difference: ally often supports a shared cause; partner shares an activity or responsibility.
colleague works in the same organization or profession; partner implies cooperation or shared stake.

usage_note: partner is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.
